reply_text:
No, I didn't use parks. I used Claude Code's own background monitors, and that's the wrong tool for anything long-running.

**Why the monitors aren't good enough:**
- They only wake me inside this one Claude Code process, and Agency can't see them.
- They expire after 30 minutes.
- They don't survive a restart.
- If you aren't watching this buffer, the "report back" is just a turn that may land unseen.

They happened to work for the short preflight waits. A real click under the debugger can sit paused at a stop for hours, and these monitors can't wait that long.

**What I'll do from here:**
- **Work I hand to the Zai staff** (the Zai token-reporting fix, and any repairs at debugger stops) goes out with `agency_send.py --mode work --park`, with the session pinned. My seat's registry session matches this REPL (`5a109aed…`), and nothing is parked now. When their jobs finish, the resume comes back into this buffer as a continuation of the same turn.
- **The click itself is the gap.** Parks wait on invoke job ids. A WM click isn't an invoke job, and a debugger stop doesn't notify anyone; it just shows up in `(stopped)`. That means nothing can wake me when the machine pauses, which is the moment that matters most.

There are two ways to close that gap. One is to have a debugger stop end the job I'm parked on, which also makes a stop show up for your assessment. The other is to have each stop write a record to the evidence store and ring a bell to whoever launched the click. I lean toward the second, because the stops get recorded as well as signalled. I'd make that change before the next click, alongside the Zai token fix.

Nothing is waiting on a monitor right now. The click is blocked on your budget renewal. I'm not tracking that renewal in any way, so tell me when it's in, or tell me to draft renewal 8 for one click.
